content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast highs.
- Underestimate downward trends after sharp price increases; model tends to overreact to recent highs.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust for delayed reaction to news or policy changes.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to overshoots in the opposite direction.
- When true price drops sharply after a peak, model often fails to recognize the trend and continues forecasting upward.
- Forecasting horizon >10 days shows increasing underestimation of downward momentum; apply stronger downward bias correction.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum; reduce forecast volatility when historical variance is low.
- Model tends to overestimate volatility in the first 5–7 days of forecast window; smooth out early forecast spikes.
